question: Should OpenClaw standardize passive root-session and trace identifiers in the core session contract, or keep richer chain tracking outside core until a plugin/API owner is selected?
rationale: Current main already has partial core parent/depth fields, but `VISION.md` cautions against turning this into an agent-hierarchy or heavy orchestration layer; source and prior discussion do not establish the permanent owner or semantics for root/trace identifiers.

options.title: Adopt a narrow core contract
options.body: Define immutable optional root and lineage-trace fields for all supported child-session creation paths, expose them through existing read surfaces, and explicitly exclude traversal, UI, and orchestration policy.

options.title: Keep chain enrichment plugin-owned
options.body: Retain current parent/depth facts and first design a documented plugin extension plus projection boundary for any root/trace metadata.

options.title: Defer the capability
options.body: Decline new lineage fields for now and keep the existing partial relationship data as the supported contract until a concrete built-in consumer justifies the API surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define immutable optional root and lineage-trace fields for all supported child-session creation paths, expose them through existing read surfaces, and explicitly exclude traversal, UI, and orchestration policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Current issue discussion and feature-history context place this person closest to the session model and gateway API boundary that would own the contract.
